solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Routine repast involving tea, endlessly sweet (10)

indicators.note: the meal takes the other pieces into its middle
the last letter of 'nice' is cut off

blocks.note: a repast is a meal; it opens as ME…AL
cha = tea, as in 'a cup of cha'
NICE without its final E

annotation.surface: Someone describes their daily tea break, where the tea is always sweetened.
annotation.walkthrough: Two pieces go inside the repast, not one. Cha is British slang for tea, from the Chinese.
annotation.definitionFit: Something mechanical is done by rote, as a matter of routine.

entries.clue: Second exercise class for depressive (4)

definitions.note: MOPE here is the noun, a gloomy person, matching 'depressive' used as a noun.

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, a second
PE = physical education, the school exercise lesson

annotation.surface: A gym timetable lists a second exercise session aimed at people with depression.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks like an ordinal, but it is the noun: 'wait a second' = 'wait a mo'.
annotation.definitionFit: A mope is a gloomy, listless person, which is what a depressive is.

entries.clue: M’s predecessor constrained by Bond showing mercy (7)

indicators.note: the letter is held inside the other word

blocks.note: cement is a bond; it wraps round the L
L comes just before M in the alphabet

annotation.surface: A spy story: the chief before M was kept in check by James Bond, who spared someone.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital B and the letter M both point to the James Bond films, but M is just a letter of the alphabet and Bond is plain cement.
annotation.definitionFit: Clement means merciful or lenient, as in the verb 'show clemency'.

entries.clue: Much sentimentality about female at Oxford ultimately useless (1,3,3,2,4)

indicators.note: the phrase for 'much' goes around the other pieces
take only the last letter of Oxford

blocks.note: a lot of = much; it opens up as A…LOT OF
F = female
used as it stands
goo is sickly sentiment
last letter of Oxford

annotation.surface: A cynic dismisses the gushing sentiment over a woman who studied at Oxford as pointless.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Much' is a three-word phrase that splits after its first word. The answer is always said ironically: it means no good at all.
annotation.definitionFit: 'A fat lot of good' is sarcastic English for something that does no good, so useless.

entries.clue: What may be melting in current century with rising speed? (3,3)

indicators.note: in a down clue the word reads upwards, so backwards

blocks.note: I is the symbol for electric current
C = century, as in cricket scores
pace = speed; it reads upwards as ECAP

annotation.surface: A question about climate change: what is melting ever faster in this century?
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as a comment on global warming, and the answer is exactly what it is talking about.
annotation.definitionFit: Polar ice caps are the familiar example of something melting as the planet warms.

entries.clue: Sign where fish are small, having lost mass (8)

indicators.note: the M for mass is dropped

blocks.note: AQUARIUM, a fish tank, minus its M
M = mass, the letter removed
S = small, as on clothing labels

annotation.surface: A notice says the fish in a tank are small ones, now that the big one has gone.
annotation.walkthrough: The fish point towards Pisces, the fish sign, but the sign is the water carrier found by way of the aquarium.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the water carrier is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

entries.clue: One does admire poachers at last catching game (4)

indicators.note: take the final letter of poachers

blocks.note: last letter of poachers
tag is the playground game of catching

annotation.surface: Someone admits a grudging admiration for poachers who finally land some game.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Does' is the plural of doe, female deer: a stag is one that admires does. Read 'does' as a verb and the definition vanishes.
annotation.definitionFit: A stag is a male deer, which would be the one admiring the does.

entries.clue: Rosenthal, a minister showing masses of brains (7)

indicators.note: the answer shows through the words that hold it

blocks.note: RosenTHAL, A MInister

annotation.surface: Someone is praising Rosenthal as a minister of great intellect.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer spans three words: the end of the name, the single A, and the start of minister.
annotation.definitionFit: The thalami are the two masses of grey matter deep in the brain; each brain has one pair.

entries.clue: Commando without experience leads soldiers in punt (5,5)

indicators.note: the first piece goes at the front
the soldiers sit inside the punt

blocks.note: green = inexperienced
a punt is a bet; it opens as BE…T
RE = Royal Engineers

annotation.surface: An untrained commando takes charge of a squad of soldiers crammed into a flat-bottomed boat.
annotation.walkthrough: A punt is a river boat, but here it is a wager. Green Berets are British Royal Marine commandos and US special forces.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the commando units are nicknamed for the colour of the caps they wear.

entries.clue: Christian VIP yet to meet maker? (7)

blocks.note: pre- = before, not yet
to meet your maker is to die; the dead are 'the late'

annotation.surface: A senior churchman who has not yet died and gone to meet God.
annotation.walkthrough: Split the answer as PRE-LATE, 'before being late', and it describes anyone still alive. The question mark flags that playful split.
annotation.definitionFit: A prelate is a high-ranking churchman such as a bishop.

entries.clue: River banks washed out around area in the dark (7)

indicators.note: the river's two ends sit either side, like banks
the word for 'washed out' is turned round

blocks.note: the Ure is a Yorkshire river; it splits as U…RE
wan = pale; turned round it gives NAW
A = area

annotation.surface: A river has burst its banks and washed away the land round an area at night.
annotation.walkthrough: 'River banks' wants to be one idea, the edges of a river; in fact 'banks' is a verb, the river enclosing the rest. The Ure is a river in Yorkshire, England.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: being kept in the dark means lacking knowledge, as if unable to see.

entries.clue: Displaced man changed ID one summer? (6,7)

indicators.note: the letters are moved out of place

blocks.note: anagram fodder
I = one, the Roman numeral

annotation.surface: A refugee has changed his identity one summer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Summer' is the season on the surface, but the question mark asks for one who sums: a machine that adds up.
annotation.definitionFit: A crossword-only sense: read 'summer' as 'one who sums', and a device that totals figures fits.

entries.clue: Team doctor stopping to help on field (4,6)

indicators.note: the doctor plugs the middle of 'help'
in an across clue, the second part is placed after the first

blocks.note: a realm is a field of activity
aid = help; it opens as A…ID
Dr = doctor

annotation.surface: The team doctor rushes onto the pitch to treat a player.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is all sport, and 'field' sounds like the pitch, but it is a sphere of interest, as in 'the realm of science'.
annotation.definitionFit: Real Madrid is a famous Spanish football team.

entries.clue: A positive result having trimmed one’s beard (3)

indicators.note: trimming a beard cuts a little off, so a letter is snipped out of the word

blocks.note: used as it stands
a WIN with its I cut out
I = one, the letter removed

annotation.surface: A man's successful outcome: he finally tidied his beard.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Beard' is the botanical sense: the bristly tuft on an ear of barley or wheat.
annotation.definitionFit: An awn is the bristle on grasses and cereals, also called the beard.

entries.clue: Completed article on Native Americans in bother (2,3,5)

blocks.note: as in 'time is up'
the definite article
the Creek are a Native American people

annotation.surface: A finished magazine piece about Native Americans who are having difficulties.
annotation.walkthrough: The Creek (the Muscogee) are a people of the southeastern United States.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom, short for 'up the creek without a paddle': stuck in a difficult situation.

entries.clue: Little darling couple has married off (6)

indicators.note: the M for married comes off

blocks.note: pet = darling, as a term of endearment
a couple is an item; drop its M
M = married, the letter removed

annotation.surface: A small, sweet pair of newlyweds heads off on honeymoon.
annotation.walkthrough: A couple who are dating are 'an item', which is the step most solvers miss.
annotation.definitionFit: Petite means small and dainty.

entries.clue: Knowing about false icon failed to impress (3,2,3)

indicators.note: the outer word goes around the other
the letters of icon are not in their true order

blocks.note: cute = shrewd, knowing; it opens as CUT…E
icon rearranged

annotation.surface: An art expert unmasks a fake religious icon that did not fool anyone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cute' in its older sense means sharp-witted, as in 'a cute move'. The answer is past tense, like 'failed'.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: a blade that makes no mark on ice has no effect, and so an argument that makes no impression.

entries.clue: Creature no longer seen in area south of large country (5,3)

indicators.note: in a down clue, the area goes below the word for large

blocks.note: great = large
A = area
the United Kingdom

annotation.surface: An animal has vanished from a region in the south of a large country.
annotation.walkthrough: 'South of' is not a compass bearing: in a down entry it just means 'written below'.
annotation.definitionFit: The great auk was a flightless seabird hunted to extinction in the 1840s.

entries.clue: Losing wings, so start to drop lower? (8)

indicators.note: the outer letters are cut away
take the first letter of drop

blocks.note: THEREFORE = so; lose its first and last letters
first letter of drop

annotation.surface: A bird losing its wings, and so beginning to drop lower.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lower' is not 'further down' but 'one that lows', a cow; the Hereford is a breed of beef cattle, named after the English city.
annotation.definitionFit: A Hereford is a cow, and cows low, so it is a lower.

entries.clue: Chap hungover, not very lively (7)

indicators.note: the V for very is taken out
the remaining letters move about

blocks.note: HUNGOVER less V
V = very, the letter removed

annotation.surface: A man with a hangover is not feeling very lively.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Chap' looks like a man but is the verb, what cold wind does to lips and hands.
annotation.definitionFit: To chap skin is to make it rough and cracked, to roughen it.

entries.clue: Mark’s daughter self-satisfied European entertains (6)

indicators.note: the pair takes the daughter in, as a host takes in a guest

blocks.note: smug = self-satisfied; it opens as SMU…G
D = daughter
E = European

annotation.surface: A man called Mark has a smug daughter who has a European partner to stay.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mark’s' reads as a person's name owning a daughter; it is the definition plus 'has'. The D goes inside SMUG before the E.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym when 'mark' is the noun: a smear or blot left by a dirty finger.

entries.clue: Gods protecting revolutionary republic for pennies (7)

indicators.note: the gods surround the republic
the country is turned round

blocks.note: dei is Latin for gods; it opens as DE…I
the Islamic Republic; turned round it gives NARI

annotation.surface: The gods shield a republic in revolution, in return for small change.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' hints at the 1979 Iranian revolution but here means 'turned round'. Old British pennies were written d, from denarius.
annotation.definitionFit: Denarii were Roman coins, and d for denarius was the symbol for the old British penny.

entries.clue: Win back theatre company with uniform parts (6)

indicators.note: the added letters split the theatre word in two

blocks.note: rep = repertory theatre; it opens as RE…P
Co = company
U is Uniform in the phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: A theatre company wins back its audience with costumed roles.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Theatre company' reads as one idea, and 'parts' as acting roles; in fact the company and uniform part REP.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: you regain, or win back, money you have lost.

entries.clue: Source of vintage puzzle does not include Times (3)

indicators.note: the letter for times is left out

blocks.note: a crux is a puzzle; drop its X
X = times, the multiplication sign

annotation.surface: A crossword clue about wine has been left out of the Times puzzle.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital T makes 'Times' look like this newspaper; it is the multiplication sign X.
annotation.definitionFit: A cru is a vineyard or wine-growing area, where a vintage comes from.

entries.clue: Pastel, once restored, reflecting different colours (10)

indicators.note: the letters are put back together in a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder

annotation.surface: An old pastel drawing, once restored, shows a range of colours.
annotation.walkthrough: The art-restoration surface fits the definition so neatly that the anagram hides in plain sight.
annotation.definitionFit: Opalescent means showing shifting milky colours like an opal.

entries.clue: Sons drink, kiss and cuddle (4)

blocks.note: S = son; 'sons' abbreviates the same way
nog is a strong ale, as in eggnog

annotation.surface: The sons have a drink and some romance.
annotation.walkthrough: Snog is British slang for a long kiss.
annotation.definitionFit: A British colloquialism for a lengthy session of kissing and embracing.

entries.clue: Earl and duke devoured by Asian land animal (7)

indicators.note: the duke ends up inside the country, as if eaten

blocks.note: E = earl
it opens as CHI…NA
D = duke

annotation.surface: Two noblemen are eaten by a wild creature in Asia.
annotation.walkthrough: Only the duke is devoured; the earl stands in front of CHINA.
annotation.definitionFit: The echidna is a spiny egg-laying mammal of Australia and New Guinea.

entries.clue: Round character extremely short in leg (7)

indicators.note: the short word goes inside the word for leg

blocks.note: the leg side in cricket is also called the on side; it opens as O…N
micro = tiny, extremely short, as in micro-skirt

annotation.surface: A plump person with very short legs.
annotation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side of the field is also the on side, so ON = leg. The Greek letter omicron is a round O.
annotation.definitionFit: Omicron is the Greek letter O, a round character in both senses.

entries.clue: Ceremonial county known to Scots (4)

blocks.note: one of England's official counties, in the southeast, known as the Garden of England
the Scots verb 'ken', to know, in its past form

annotation.surface: A formal English county that the Scots have heard of.
annotation.walkthrough: A ceremonial county is one of England's official counties with a Lord Lieutenant. Scots 'ken' survives in 'beyond my ken'; its past form is kent.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses: a definition by example for the county, and a regional Scots use for the past participle.

entries.clue: Leading swimmer smoked with Carol outside (10)

indicators.note: the song goes around the fish

blocks.note: to carol is to sing; it opens as S…ING
a kipper is a smoked herring

annotation.surface: The top swimmer lit up a cigarette with a woman called Carol outside.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital C makes Carol a woman's name; it is the verb, to sing. 'Swimmer' is a crossword word for fish.
annotation.definitionFit: Skippering a team or ship means leading it.
